header: INTERACTIVE · A MESSAGE, END TO END
note: It goes to another continent, and the reply lands before you have put the phone down.
The bytes become a radio wave, and cross the room to your router.
Voltage steps on copper, until the cabinet turns them into light.
The message stops at the app's data center, a few hundred kilometres from your phone.
6,600 km of glass on the sea floor, laid by a consortium. The app's company only leases fibre pairs inside it.
Inland, out to a tower, and back into radio for the last kilometre.
None of the companies along the way coordinated for this message, and none of them knows the whole path it took.
